context: The opening year of CShapes’ global time series. This snapshot shows the political units and dependencies represented by the dataset at its starting point; it is not a complete inventory of every sovereignty claim.

contextSources.title: CShapes 2.1 data release

context: A year-end view around the Spanish–American War and the Treaty of Paris, signed in December. The treaty’s territorial provisions took effect later, so this snapshot captures a transition rather than a settled postwar map.

contextSources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian: The Spanish–American War

context: The First World War began in Europe in 1914. At year end, older empires still covered large areas even as conflict was changing the political map.

contextSources.title: Library of Congress: World War I timeline

context: The armistice year brought the breakup of Austria-Hungary and the emergence of successor states. CShapes records several of these political changes in its 1918 year-end snapshot.

contextSources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian: Hungary

context: The Treaty of Versailles entered into force on 10 January 1920, formalizing important postwar territorial arrangements. The map is a December snapshot, after that settlement took effect.

contextSources.title: U.S. Government Publishing Office: Treaty of Versailles

context: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed in July 1923 and established the postwar settlement with Turkey. The year-end map reflects the political geography after the treaty.

contextSources.title: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Treaty of Lausanne

context: Germany invaded Poland in September 1939; Soviet forces entered from the east later that month, and the country was partitioned. CShapes represents political units and territorial periods, not the full military front line.

contextSources.title: U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum: Invasion of Poland, Fall 1939

context: World War II ended in Europe in 1945. Germany was divided into Allied occupation zones; those administrative zones are not all represented as separate boundaries in this dataset.

contextSources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian: Division of Germany, 1949

context: The People’s Republic of China was proclaimed on 1 October. In Europe, the Federal Republic and German Democratic Republic were established during the year, after occupation-zone administration.

contextSources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian: The Chinese Revolution of 1949
U.S. Office of the Historian: Division of Germany, 1949

context: Morocco and Tunisia became independent in 1956, while Sudan had become independent earlier that year. This snapshot captures several shifts away from colonial rule in North Africa.

contextSources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian: Morocco recognized as independent
U.S. Office of the Historian: Morocco and Tunisia

context: Seventeen African countries became independent during 1960. The United Nations General Assembly adopted its Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples in December.

contextSources.title: United Nations: General Assembly resolution 1514 (XV)

context: Singapore became an independent republic on 9 August 1965 after separating from Malaysia. The map’s boundaries show state units, not the full political circumstances of the separation.

contextSources.title: Singapore Statutes Online: Republic of Singapore Independence Act 1965

context: Bangladesh declared independence in March 1971 and became a new state after the Bangladesh Liberation War. This year-end snapshot includes Bangladesh as a separate political unit.

contextSources.title: Bangladesh Laws: Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

context: A major year in the end of Portuguese rule in Africa: Angola, Mozambique, Cape Verde, and São Tomé and Príncipe became independent during 1975. The year-end view reflects the resulting political changes.

contextSources.title: United Nations Yearbook 1975

context: Zimbabwe became independent on 18 April 1980. The change followed the end of white-minority rule in Southern Rhodesia and is visible in this year-end political snapshot.

contextSources.title: United Nations Security Council document S/14064

context: The Soviet Union dissolved at the end of 1991, with former republics entering the international system as independent states. The dataset records boundaries and status periods, not every recognition dispute.

contextSources.title: United Nations: Russian Federation letter on continued membership

context: Eritrea declared independence in 1993, and Czechoslovakia separated into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on 1 January. Both changes appear in the CShapes political-unit record.

contextSources.title: United Nations: UN Observer Mission to Verify the Referendum in Eritrea

context: Timor-Leste became independent on 20 May 2002 after a United Nations-administered transition. The map shows the resulting separate state boundary.

contextSources.title: United Nations Security Council: Statement on Timor-Leste independence

context: Montenegro declared independence in June 2006, ending the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro. CShapes includes the resulting state split in its year-end snapshot.

contextSources.title: United Nations: Member States and former Yugoslavia

context: South Sudan became independent on 9 July 2011. The year-end map shows it as a separate state from Sudan; its northern border remained contested in some areas.

contextSources.title: United Nations: South Sudan
